tools.name: list_assets
tools.description: List every asset the swap form knows: slug (the network is part of the slug, e.g. usdt-trc20, usdt-erc20), ticker, network, confirmations, the name of the extra id (memo, tag, payment ID) where the chain uses one, and whether the asset is available right now. Use it first, to turn a coin name into t

tools.name: list_routes
tools.description: List the routes that have their own page on sablebolt.io: from and to slugs, a curated core, and whether both sides are available right now. Use it to find a documented route or to link its page. Not the limit of what can be swapped: any two assets from list_assets can be swapped through get_limits,

tools.name: get_limits
tools.description: Get the minimum and maximum amount for one route, in the asset you send. Call it before get_quote or create_swap: an amount outside the limits is refused by both. For the estimate itself use get_quote. With mode=private the swap runs as two legs through an intermediate coin and the limits cover both

tools.name: get_quote
tools.description: Get a floating estimate for a route and amount: amountTo, networkFee (taken out of the payout), receiveAmount (what arrives after that fee) and rate. Use it to tell a person what they would receive or to size a create_swap. Not for the allowed range (get_limits) and it creates nothing. The estimate

tools.name: validate_address
tools.description: Check whether an address has the right format for one asset. Use it on both addresses before get_swap_page_link or create_swap. tools.name: get_swap_status
tools.description: Get the status of one swap by its id: status and stage (1 waiting for the deposit, 2 confirming, 3 exchanging, 4 sending, 5 finished), rateType (floating or fixed) with payTill (a fixed order's deposit deadline), deposit and payout addresses, amounts, both transaction hashes and the status page URL;

tools.description: Get the link to the page where a person completes the swap, with the route and, optionally, the amount prefilled; also the page's markdown twin and the hand-off rule. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_swap_status, get_swap_page_link · Private data: get_limits, get_quote, validate_address, create_swap, get_swap_page_link · Public sink: get_limits, create_swap, get_swap_page_link · Destructive: validate_address.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_swap_status, get_swap_page_link · Private data: get_limits, get_quote, validate_address, create_swap, get_swap_page_link · Public sink: get_limits, create_swap, get_swap_page_link · Destructive: validate_address

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "list_assets" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
